correctness.rationale: Global convex averaging is legitimate for every symmetric stochastic feasible P since SLEM=||P-J||₂. The exact 2×2 Fourier blocks give all invariant eigenvalues. Strict monotonicity in spoke weight and strict convexity of the positive-mode lower bound establish its unique optimizer. An exact identity shows the worst negative eigenvalue has smaller modulus, while the zero-mode eigenvalue is bounded. The argument covers every integer m≥3. Seven algebraic identities and 41 actual matrices were verified, with 3280 feasible invariant perturbation and 770 feasible noninvariant sampling checks; numerical checks are not used to prove the universal quantifiers.

evidence: The 2004/2007 general graph framework allows symmetry averaging and Fourier analysis, but supplies no closed formula for the sunlet cycle-spoke minimax problem.
The 2010 cyclic pseudo-distance-regular graphs have no single pendant leaf on each core and the 2025 clique-lift reduction has complete internal clique fibers.
The explicit new proof uses strict convexity of a first-Fourier-mode lower bound followed by a nontrivial inequality controlling the opposite spectral edge: rho²-(b²+4a²)=z(z+2)(2-z²)/D²>0.

The m=3 boundary case coincides with a clique core K3 with one pendant leaf per core vertex and is already obtained by the earlier clique-corona formula; that formula does not apply to cycle cores C_m for m≥4 because C_m is not complete.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The claimed global sunlet result follows from the established convex framework only after deriving and solving a new two-parameter spectral problem and verifying that no other Fourier mode dominates. It is not a direct specialization of the closed formulas for different graphs. Residual risk is a not-yet-indexed specialist paper with exactly this graph. The m=3 overlap is explicitly credited and does not establish the new m≥4 cyclic-core family.

evidence: The 2007 Boyd–Diaconis–Parrilo–Xiao manuscript treats wheel graphs in §5.3.3 (one central hub) and a repeated six-vertex cyclic graph in §5.3.6, neither the one-leaf-per-core sunlet.
The explicit proposed weights depend on the cycle first Fourier frequency through z=√2 sin(π/m) and are not obtained by a parameter rename of a cycle-only optimum.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For equivalent formulations the underlying adjacency/support graph must coincide, or the prior theorem must cover arbitrary graph with an evaluated output. The wheel and cyclic examples have different supports; the general SDP representation has no analytic sunlet solution. Searching formulations using corona, sunlet, ring with leaves, and symmetric edge-weight optimization yielded no exact equivalent among inspected materials.

originality.rationale: An exact all-size SLEM formula and optimal two-edge-orbit weights for the sunlet corona are not a stated or directly implied special case of the inspected graph-optimization treatments: the general SDP method is not an evaluated solution, the wheel has one hub rather than individual leaves, cyclic K-partite pseudo-distance-regular networks have complete interlayer connections without pendant leaves, and clique lifting requires different fiber connections. The result is considered original on currently inspected evidence with residual bibliographic risk. The m=3 triangle-core member overlaps an existing clique-with-one-leaf classification; originality concerns the infinite nonclique-core m≥4 family.
residual_risks: A specialist article or thesis not indexed by the searched sources may have independently solved the sunlet graph.

value.rationale: The fully determined global fastest-mixing value on a nonregular unicyclic infinite graph family is a motivated graph-weight design invariant, not a generic convex-program restatement. The formula supplies explicit optimal cycle/spoke probabilities, proves that the core has no holding, and yields sharp 1/m spoke scaling and 1/m² gap scaling. The solved extremal statement and negative-mode certificate explain a concrete nontrivial topology-induced mixing slowdown and support future comparison with other corona and decorated-cycle graphs.
